#2773. Tech Report: What does the blue snowflake icon mean for your Tesla battery?

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (718 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: What does the blue snowflake icon mean for your Tesla battery?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Less available range, weaker regenerative braking and slower charging are all possible when that blue snowflake appears.
  • Tesla isn't sending you a little Easter egg for the holidays with that tiny blue snowflake that pops up next to the battery indicator.
  • According to recent reports, you don't need to second-guess how much juice the EV has left 'cause Tesla marks the unavailable part in blue on the battery meter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less available range, weaker regenerative braking and slower charging are all possible when that blue snowflake appears.

Tesla isn't sending you a little Easter egg for the holidays with that tiny blue snowflake that pops up next to the battery indicator. You're not getting a heads-up about the icy roads ahead either. Instead, that little indicator is actually telling you about your battery feeling the chills too. And when the battery gets cold enough to throw a blue snowflake light, some of its stored energy temporarily becomes unavailable.

According to recent reports, you don't need to second-guess how much juice the EV has left 'cause Tesla marks the unavailable part in blue on the battery meter. But that temporarily disabled energy is usable again once the battery warms up as you drive around. Now, don't confuse the little snowflake indicator with the power your Tesla has lost overnight parked in your garage. The energy shown in blue on the battery meter is just the energy that's temporarily out of reach due to the cold.

But even with a warmed-up battery, the cold will still bite a chunk out of your range. Keeping the cabin warm and toasty, combined with cold weather terrain depending on where you're driving, tends to take up more power than usual even for the regular gas-guzzler.

In a recent development, other than some lost range on your EV, that festive blue snowflake also changes how your Tesla runs. Things like how long the car takes to charge and even that powerful acceleration could all feel a bit different. Regenerative braking also feels quite different if you're used to slowing down by taking your foot off the accelerator.

Recent findings suggest that the whole idea behind regenerative braking is that when you lift off the accelerator pedal, energy that would otherwise be lost gets sent back to the battery. When the battery is on the colder side, it can't absorb that energy as it does in normal conditions, so expect your Tesla's regen effect to feel much weaker approaching a red light.

If you own a Model 3, check to see if your variant has a setting that allows stronger deceleration when regenerative braking is limited. Try to find the Apply Brakes When Regenerative Braking Is Limited option in Controls > Dynamics. Having this function on tells the car to use its normal, mechanical brakes to mimic full regenerative braking. Again, your ability to select this totally depends on the model and the software version running on your Tesla.

Your Tesla might even show a separate icon that specifically tells you when regenerative braking isn't fully available. This looks a bit like a broken green brake disc with an electricity symbol inside. Either way, you're better off keeping that foot ready to hit the brakes yourself just to be safe.

According to recent reports, feel like a grumpy old Grinch and want that blue snowflake off? Well, Tesla won't let you do that manually, and the icon only goes away when your car's battery warms up again. Driving around or charging it should help, or instead of leaving the car in the cold, set up preconditioning for the battery. The way to do this is through Controls > Schedule on either the car's touchscreen or your Tesla app. Remotely turning on cabin climate controls is just what that high-voltage battery needs to get warmed up.

Industry observers note that the smart thing to do here, if possible, is to keep the EV plugged in so all that preconditioning happens while the car's battery is receiving power continuously. Otherwise, you'll start the day with less charge than you were hoping to drive with, kind of defeating the whole purpose. If you want to fill up the EV faster with a Tesla Supercharger, start by setting it as your destination. This will get your EV's battery all warmed up and ready to be plugged in for fast charging with fewer delays.

It has been revealed that there's no real indicator of what temperature actually triggers the snowflake icon, and Tesla hasn't given a timeframe for when it goes away either. The firm does, however, recommend that you gear up your car's climate settings to activate at least 30 to 45 minutes before leaving.

Tech Report: Genesis Introduces Hybrids at the LA Auto Show, EREV Coming in 2027

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Korean luxury automaker Genesis debuted its first hybrid models this week, debuting fresh powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show.
  • The hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies.
  • Sources indicate that the G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Korean luxury automaker Genesis debuted its first hybrid models this week, debuting fresh powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show. The manufacturer says the electrified system is both more efficient and more powerful than the current nonhybrid versions. For buyers who want a more battery-focused experience, Genesis teased an upcoming 640-mile extended-range electric vehicle due to arrive in early 2027.

The hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies. Hybrids, in particular, have attracted attention because they behave like traditional combustion cars: There’s no need to install home charging hardware or change familiar driving and refueling habits. Just get in and reap better fuel economy with every mile.

Sources indicate that the G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain. Genesis claims the system is 16% more powerful than the gasoline-only version, outputting 347 horsepower and 391 pound-feet of torque. A latest liquid-cooled battery pack improves thermal management and allows higher maximum discharge than Hyundai Motor Group’s previous air-cooled hybrid batteries, boosting performance. Both models use a seven-speed automatic transmission adapted to work with the electric motor’s regenerative braking.

According to recent reports, genesis hasn’t unveiled official fuel economy estimates, but notes the G80 Hybrid is 30% more efficient than the standard model, while the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient. Based on current EPA figures, my math puts them in the ballpark of 30 mpg and 27 mpg, respectively. Any improvement is good, but those aren’t exactly earth-shattering gains. We’ll have to wait for the official ratings to be sure.

Recent findings suggest that each hybrid can be toggled into a silent EV mode for short distances — good for gliding into a driveway, garage or parking deck without waking the neighbors. However, without a plug, all the energy in the battery ultimately comes from the gas tank.

A new Stay Mode lets owners run the climate control and infotainment without starting the engine for around 30 minutes. I like to think of it as the “moment of zen in the driveway before you have to go inside and face responsibility” mode, or maybe the “eating lunch in your car” mode. It’s similar to Toyota’s My Room Mode on its hybrids.

Aside from the powertrain, the G80 and GV80 Hybrids are largely identical to their combustion counterparts. Hybrid-specific touches include a three-dimensional G-Matrix grille inlay redesigned for these models, as well as newly introduced exterior colors.

It has been revealed that inside, a 27-inch OLED display combining the instrument cluster and navigation stretches halfway across the dashboard. Tech features include Digital Key 2 Premium, which lets owners use their phone instead of a key fob to unlock and start the car, and active road noise cancellation. Genesis’ driver-assistance suite is headlined by the Highway Drive Assist 2 steering assistance system and the Remote Smart Parking Assist 2, which enables automatic parking with the driver inside or just nearby the car.

In a recent development, prices for the sedan and SUV haven’t been declared. Final specifications and EPA fuel economy figures are expected closer to the early 2027 launch window.

According to recent reports, my cynical side says that these new models are just Genesis doing what Toyota has done since the RX 400h debuted in 2004. (To be fair, Genesis didn’t become an independent brand until 2015, so its rival has a bit of a head start.) In practical terms, the move brings Hyundai Motor Group’s luxury brand into parity with other group members and luxury car competitors that have rolled out updated hybrids over the last year, and meets customers’ increasing demand for more energy-efficient cars where they are.

In addition to its first hybrid sedan and SUV, Genesis executives announced that the brand will expand the availability of its wild-styled, high-performance GV60 Magma full-electric SUV to more states and markets to meet higher-than-expected demand.

In a recent development, at the debut event in LA, the brand also teased an upcoming extended-range EV — an EV with an onboard gasoline generator, essentially a very advanced plug-in hybrid — set to launch in early 2027. The EREV model is targeting over 640 miles before its “all-fresh high-performance battery” and gas tank both run dry, but Genesis didn’t give further details about the upcoming model.

Editor’s note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Limited editions, sweepstakes rewards and specific game bundle consoles far exceed their initial price.
  • Most people can recognize an original PlayStation or Nintendo 64 at a glance, but some variations of common consoles are much less familiar.
  • It has been revealed that if you have an older console tucked away in a closet, it could be worth checking which edition you own.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Limited editions, sweepstakes rewards and specific game bundle consoles far exceed their initial price.

Most people can recognize an original PlayStation or Nintendo 64 at a glance, but some variations of common consoles are much less familiar. Perhaps they were made for a limited promotion, released exclusively in Japan or were given away through a contest. Some consoles never made it to stores, like the Nintendo PlayStation prototype acquired by the National Videogame Museum.

It has been revealed that if you have an older console tucked away in a closet, it could be worth checking which edition you own. A system you might have considered to be obsolete and boring could be worth more than you think.

To gauge how rare these editions are, we looked at production numbers, limited giveaways and collector records. For resale values, we prioritized documented sales and price-guide estimates.

The Nintendo 64 came in plenty of colors (and inspired Analogue 3D colors based on N64 prototypes), but this gold version is one you probably didn't see on store shelves. The Toys "R" Us-exclusive edition featured a metallic gold console with matching controllers, which was much flashier than the usual gray and black hardware.

While it's not a production total, Video Game Authority's (VGA) December 2025 census listed only nine examples of this variant. A gold console graded 80 (out of 100) NM (near-mint) by VGA, with two matching controllers, sold for $3,250 in January 2026. Recent ungraded sales tracked by PriceCharting include loose consoles for around $140 to $425, while those still in the box have sold for $1,750 to $3,000 in 2026.

In a recent development, if you grew up during the Pokémon '90s boom, you might remember the Pikachu Edition Nintendo 64; it was released as a Toys "R" Us exclusive in North America. ‘The show is starting soon. Please turn on your headphones.’

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Auracast broadcasts are an integral part of the storytelling in this off-Broadway show about love, connections, and hearing loss.
  • Auracast broadcasts are an integral part of the storytelling in this off-Broadway show about love, connections, and hearing loss.
  • Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Auracast broadcasts are an integral part of the storytelling in this off-Broadway show about love, connections, and hearing loss.

Auracast broadcasts are an integral part of the storytelling in this off-Broadway show about love, connections, and hearing loss.

Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse. As we filter to our seats, ushers hand each person a black drawstring bag with a pair of wired headphones connected to a small Auracast receiver. Then, soon after the play begins, we’re instructed to put them on.

The headphones are an integral storytelling tool of Love Me — a one-man show from the minds of stand-up comedian and former Saturday Night Live writer Drew Michael and director Prashanth Venkataramanujam. It’s a show about love and the bid for connection, told in five chapters about different relationships in Michael’s life, bound by the threads of his hearing loss and self-discovery.

Recent findings suggest that love Me’s experimental sound design is possible thanks to Auracast, a technology based on Bluetooth that can broadcast a high-quality audio stream to any number of nearby devices. As the show follows Michael from childhood through adulthood, sound designer Daniel Kluger uses the headphones in combination with the theater speakers to create experiences that wouldn’t be possible with a traditional setup. Tinnitus ringing and hearing test tones play in the music between sections as subtle clues as the show builds to Michael’s epiphany about his hearing loss. Kluger also explores the world through varying levels of sonic clarity. Sound playing through the theater’s speakers is sometimes intentionally muffled, which is then further dulled by the headphones, giving the audience a sense of what Michael is hearing in those moments.

But one sound that stays clear and pristine is Michael’s inner monologue, heard in the headphones throughout the show. The inner monologue consists of both prerecorded tracks and the live feed from Michael’s microphone on stage as he talks back and forth with himself. “Any time you’re in my head — anything in the headphones is coming through clearly,” Michael tells me after the show. “[We’re] trying to also highlight that the appeal of the inner world is such that it’s the highest fidelity space for this person. It’s more comfortable.”.

Industry observers note that the different sound sources and treatments of the sound can lead to intentionally confusing scenes for the audience. During one, where Michael is doing a stand-up set at a comedy club, three sounds compete for attention: The theater speakers play the crowd’s reactions (including a heckler whose voice is sometimes muffled and sometimes clear); his prerecorded inner monologue reacting to the crowd plays in the headphones; and on stage, Michael is performing the set, with his mic muffled so our focus is on his inner monologue. It’s one of the definitive moments where the audience feels the constant concentration necessary to parse what’s happening when sounds aren’t clear and become overwhelming.

Industry observers note that but the biggest impact comes during a climactic scene the sound design has been building toward, a realization that also incorporates the visuals of a series of Michael’s audiograms over the years. “I had this massive breakthrough about the whole history of what I’ve been doing — the cognitive labor, the invisible to myself labor that was affecting every single minute of my life,” Michael notes. “That was a huge moment.”.

That’s when the audience is instructed to remove the headphones we’ve been wearing for nearly the entire show. As Michael comes to the recognition of his relationship with his hearing loss and the clarity of mind that gives him, what we’ve become used to for the entire show’s experience — the headphones — are now gone, as is that literal weight from our heads. It’s an emotional moment, one that I’ve thought about multiple times since seeing the show.

It also leads into the final act, where Michael begins to understand his own Deaf identity. “The deafness is not the culprit, it’s the denial of it.” he tells me. “My hearing presently has never been worse, but I’ve never been more self-affirmed or self-actualized or felt happier in myself. It’s a misconception, I think, about deafness as a tragedy, deafness as a deficit, deafness as a burden, deafness as something that plagues a person.”.

Industry observers note that the ability of Auracast to broadcast an audio stream that any number of headphones can connect to is what made Love Me a possibility. Any Auracast headphones can connect to the audience broadcast — I brought along the Nothing Pro 1 to test the ability and connected to the audience broadcast channel in seconds — but I used the provided Auri receiver and Austrian Audio headset for the performance. The show’s sound was designed with those in mind, and I didn’t want the differing isolation of the Nothing headphones to affect the intent of the experience.

It has been revealed that love Me is presented in partnership with Deaf West Theatre, which supports Deaf-centered storytelling in theatrical productions. In addition to the audience Auracast feed, there’s one for consumers of hearing aids and cochlear implants that’s designed for compliance with those devices, and iPads with captions are also available. During the performance, Michael connects to his own broadcast channel with Auracast-enabled Phonak Eon Sphere hearing aids. “We talked about using in-ear monitors, but if I use an in-ear monitor, then I don’t have amplification from my environment, so then I lose contact with the audience,” Michael says. “These function as two things: They’re hearing aids and also in-ear monitors.”.

Sources indicate that love Me relies on the Auracast technology to tell its story, but it isn’t a story about hearing technology. The technology is there to tell the story of connection and discovery of identity. “I think right now … there are two things that are at odds — the hearing aid and audiological tech side of deafness and then the cultural identity side of deafness,” Michael states. Technological improvements, like cochlear implants and hearing aids, are cited as one of the reasons schools for the deaf have been on the decline, which leads to kids being mainstreamed (put into regular public schools) and losing out on Deaf history and culture. “I’m not against the tech,” Michael says, “I just think tech and Deaf identity should be a marriage rather than a divide.”.

And that collaboration is why Love Me works as well as it does. The Auracast technology is there both for accessibility — in the same way it’s already used in other performances, lectures, or announcement systems — and to uplift the show’s story of love, acceptance, and acknowledgement of one’s own Deaf identity. It’s an inventive use of the technology that carries with it a powerful message.

#2765. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: What are the key differences?

Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: What are the key differences?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The cheaper AirPods 5 have less capabilities than the AirPods Pro 3.
  • Industry observers note that while Apple's white earbuds look similar, the AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 differ in design, charging options, capabilities and battery life.
  • Sources indicate that let's begin with the differences in appearances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The cheaper AirPods 5 have less capabilities than the AirPods Pro 3.

Industry observers note that while Apple's white earbuds look similar, the AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 differ in design, charging options, capabilities and battery life. The AirPods 5 come in two options (the base $129 model and the $149 model), while the Apple AirPods Pro 3 have one option that costs $249.

Sources indicate that let's begin with the differences in appearances. AirPods 5 have a slightly more oval-shaped bud and are solid earbuds without ear tips, designed to pop inside your ear and fit with a gentle twist. AirPods Pro 3 carry replaceable silicon ear tips that seal themselves inside the ear canal. The seal improves music playback fidelity and blocks more external noise. AirPods Pro 3 include five ear tip sizes so you can find the right fit, though other options exist, particularly for smaller ears.

In a recent development, before diving into more differences, these products do have some similarities. Both AirPods support Active Noise Cancellation (ANC), partly through new multiport acoustic architecture on AirPods 5. Both models use Apple's H2 chip which improves music playback and powers popular features. These include Personalized Spatial Audio with head tracking, Voice Isolation and studio-quality recording, Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, and Live Translation, when available. Both offer IP57 durability: they are dust resistant and should continue to work if submerged in up to 1 meter (3.3 feet) of fresh water for a short time.

Apple promises that the $129 AirPods 5 will keep going for up to four hours on one charge with ANC active (five hours with the $149 set). AirPods Pro 3 earbuds provide eight hours of music playback with ANC.

AirPods have always shipped with a protective case that doubles up as charging stations for the buds. You'll get an hour of playback if you put them in the case for 5 minutes.

It has been revealed that there's a difference in the battery capacity provided by the cases. The entry-level AirPods 5 case provides 20 hours and powers over USB-C. The $149 model reaches 22 hours and supports wireless charging. AirPods Pro 3 also offer both wireless and USB-C charging and promise 24 hours of battery life.

One final difference concerns Apple's Find My system which will help you track down a lost set of AirPods. With both AirPods, cases that support wireless charging also carry speakers that can make a noise to help you find them when mislaid. The case provided with the $129 AirPods 5 lacks this. Find My is improved with AirPods Pro 3, which supports precise tracking.

If you need Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) to suppress external noise, you're in luck, as both AirPods variants provide it. However, AirPods Pro 3 are more efficient because they use silicon ear tips which seal the ear canal, blocking external noise.

In a recent development, airPods Pro 3 provide some unique health-related features you don't find in AirPods 5, too. For example, AirPods Pro 3 provide heart rate sensing during workouts, which AirPods 5 do not. They also offer regulatory-approved hearing-related features: The short Hearing Test builds a profile for your hearing which the Hearing Aid feature uses to amplify external sound for people with hearing loss.

Another difference is that you can swipe the stalk of the AirPods to increase or lower volume on AirPods Pro 3 and the $149 AirPods 5 but not on the entry-level $129 Airpods 5.

Summing up, if you want efficient ANC, excellent music playback and sophisticated health features, choose the AirPods Pro 3. Otherwise, you'll get more from the $149 AirPods 5 than from the base $129 model.

GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them.
  • The global food system is ultimately driven by demand.
  • With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our upcoming research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land.

The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access.

With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses.

The biggest effects, however, occurred when reduced calorie intake was combined with a shift toward healthier diets. In this scenario, up to 7 million deaths could be avoided each year by 2050, while around 46 million hectares of agricultural land would have become available for other uses. This suggests that alongside weight-loss medicines, we need to make healthier options more widely available, affordable, and more appealing.

Food systems are interconnected across countries. If demand falls in one part of the world, this can affect farming, trade, and food prices elsewhere, with consequences for people who are not taking the medications at all.

Lower demand from GLP-1 users, for instance, could make food cheaper. That sounds positive, but cheaper food could also encourage greater consumption among non-users, offsetting some of the intended benefit. The effects of widespread GLP-1 use, in other words, cannot be understood just by looking at individual patients’ weight loss. They ripple through the global food system.

It’s tempting to read these findings as an argument for putting more people on weight-loss medication. That would miss the bigger picture.

In a recent development, obesity has often been framed as a “lifestyle disease,” blaming individual people for not having enough willpower. But diets are shaped by what food is available, what it costs, how it’s marketed, where shops are located, and what’s most convenient. In many high-income countries, it is remarkably easy to consume large amounts of cheap, energy-dense food. Society tells people to make healthier choices while surrounding them with an environment that often encourages the opposite.

The UK government-commissioned national food strategy, finalized in 2021, made this point clearly: improving diets can’t simply be about asking individuals to choose better. The wider food environment needs to change to make the better choice the easy one.

Our findings shouldn’t be taken to mean that people living with obesity have a responsibility to lose weight to reduce the environmental impacts of food production. Rather, our research examines the wider consequences that changes in food demand could have across the food system.

It has been revealed that A healthier diet is not necessarily just a diet with fewer calories. It could mean more fruit, vegetables, and other nutritious foods, alongside less excessive consumption of foods linked to poor health. These changes affect not only human health but also agriculture, land use, and the environment.

Rather than asking whether GLP-1 medications or healthier diets are the answer, let’s ask how they can work together. Imagine a food system where healthier foods are affordable and accessible, unhealthy options aren’t relentlessly promoted, agricultural policy supports nutritious and sustainable production, and people who need medical treatment can access it. That combination could be far more powerful than any single intervention.

Recent findings suggest that GLP-1 medicines can play an important role in tackling obesity, but they shouldn’t become a technological fix that allows the wider food system to escape scrutiny. They can help people eat less in an unhealthy food environment, but the long-term goal should be to make it easier and more affordable to have a healthier, more sustainable diet.

The remarkable thing about GLP-1 medications may not be that they change how much food people eat. It may be that they show us, with fresh clarity, just how closely human health, food production, and environmental health are connected, and how much could be gained if we tackled all three together.

Roslyn Henry is Lecturer, School of Biological Sciences, University of Aberdeen and Peter Alexander is Professor of Global Food Systems, University of Edinburgh.

Andrew Garfield on Becoming Sam Altman in ‘Artificial’: ‘I’m Dying to Understand This Person’

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.
  • Rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec.
  • According to recent reports, garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.

Rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec. 25 release. The biopic follows the rise of OpenAI, focusing on Altman’s relationships — particularly with his cofounder Ilya Sutskever (Yura Borisov) — as he relentlessly pursues success amid Silicon Valley’s artificial intelligence power struggle.

According to recent reports, garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set. His mission as an actor is to get to the “central truths” of who a person is, he said, “and try to merge my soul with theirs. And like all of us, Sam has so many facets.”.

That includes physical traits. Garfield says he had to lose weight and change his gait and voice to try to match Altman’s. The semblance is striking. From his bouncy stride to his clipped, gravelly speech, Garfield effortlessly emulates the Altman we’ve seen in interviews and Congressional testimonies. It’s a remarkable transformation — down to the sly, coaxing glint in his eyes — showcasing the breadth of Garfield’s acting talent.

Industry observers note that but it goes beyond physicality. Garfield had to dig deep internally to find elements “that felt like they were a match” with Altman, he noted. The result is an astonishingly believable portrayal of a multidimensional figure, at once pensive and inscrutable.

Recent findings suggest that “There is a responsibility,” Garfield told me. “I take it very, very seriously to play any character, but particularly someone who’s alive, someone who’s pretty much my age. But also, maybe the greater responsibility is making sure that we interrogate these human beings that are leading our world into the next chapter, it seems.”.

“And it feels like our job as storytellers to reflect the times we’re in,” he added, “and no better way of doing that than by looking at the human beings — their personal relationships, their souls, all the diamond facets of their souls — and interrogate the people that have the power over our culture right now.”.

Artificial explores OpenAI’s rise through a rather bleak lens, with questions of moral responsibility and safety looming over the protagonists as they navigate the organization’s success. The film is laced with dark satire, which offers moments of levity amid otherwise weighty meditations on the technology’s long-term impact.

In one scene, when Sutskever is asked about the difference between AI and artificial general intelligence, which can theoretically match or even surpass human ability, he plainly responds, “It’s like how rocket ships are different from scooters.” He goes on to tell his cohorts that this is achievable “in your lifetime — well, maybe not yours or yours or yours,” as he points to the less youthful figures in the room. Moments like these elicited generous laughter from the audience.

Director Luca Guadagnino, known for deeply character-driven stories, such as Challengers and Call Me by Your Name, noted he was following the news about Sam Altman’s temporary ousting from OpenAI in 2023 and was fascinated by the “Shakespearean feud” leading to that moment. Guadagnino applies his signature character-centric approach to OpenAI’s story, relying on slow, measured beats, piercing close-ups and suspenseful music to relay the stakes of each pivotal moment.

Industry observers note that “It’s never about the object; it’s always about the people,” Guadagnino mentioned during a panel discussion after the screening. “It’s not about AGI or AI. It’s about the conflict between worldview and way of being, embodied by people that clash or fight for the vision they have.”.

He also said, “The point for me was more about trying to understand: How did the possibility of an incredible technology that can help all of us turn into the opportunity to get power in your hands and to become self-entitled?”.

It has been revealed that garfield is no stranger to portraying prominent figures in the tech world, having played Eduardo Saverin, Facebook’s co-founder and former chief financial officer, in 2010’s The Social Network. On the surface, Artificial seems like a spiritual successor, recounting another defining moment in the tech industry. But the films differ in both tone and approach, with Artificial trading rapid-fire drama for a darker, more existential theme that occasionally ventures into more technical territory. What the films do share is a focus on bold, forceful personalities.

“From that experience, I suppose, I was very curious about what it takes to win in this particular late-stage capitalist world that we’re in with these emerging technologies,” Garfield said during the panel discussion. “What does it take to hold Sauron’s Ring of Power and not be completely burnt up by it? Is it possible to not completely lose yourself to that overwhelming, exponentially growing possibility and power?”.

Comic relief also arrives in the form of Ike Barinholtz playing OpenAI cofounder and tech mogul Elon Musk. By portraying him as a brutish, aloof figure who saunters in and out of rooms on a whim, he effectively underscores the absurdity of perceived importance and status. Almost every on-screen moment generated a murmur of laughter in the audience.

“I think we’re all fascinated by these cultural, iconic figures who are leading us into this next stage of culture and society,” Garfield told the crowd. “They’re kind of kids. They’re kind of slightly stuck in an early developmental place, and that felt like a really crucial part of Luca’s telling of this story.”.

Industry observers note that in fact, he added, “[Guadagnino] would say to us, ‘This is a John Hughes movie. This is a high school, screwball comedy, just with slightly higher stakes — mixed in with a little bit of Invasion of the Body Snatchers.’ A very key part of this is that these are all kind of adolescent, high-school-minded people.”.

Even the way Garfield portrays Altman flippantly perching on couches and sitting cross-legged on tabletops while donning sunglasses — including during serious conversations about the future of OpenAI — was deeply researched.

It has been revealed that “We had amazing consultants and researchers that work with us that gave us lots of information that’s not quite in the public arena about our characters,” Garfield mentioned. “And Sam is someone who apparently would always sit like he was crisscross applesauce at play school, nursery school [or] kindergarten.”.

In a recent development, ultimately, Artificial poses an open question about where society is headed and whether those at the helm are equipped to lead the charge. Amid weighty explorations of AI’s ramifications, the film paints a haunting, revelatory portrait of the cunning, mercurial figures making decisions that shape our world.

For Garfield, this presented an opportunity to dive deep into a figure like Altman, who, despite his prominence, remains largely elusive in the public eye.

“I just wanted to tell this story and actually uncover for myself, excavate for myself, who is this person?” Garfield told me. “I’m dying to understand this person, and I get to try to understand this person, maybe more than anyone else has ever really tried to. And it feels like a gift to me.”.

#2761. Does old computer hardware ever become truly useless?

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (621 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Does old computer hardware ever become truly useless?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While degradation is an obvious problem for PC parts, it's a loss of compatibility that you really have to worry about.
  • According to recent reports, despite the massive cost sinks that go into building a solid PC, many of the parts can easily be reused.
  • Recent findings suggest that PC parts aren't only great for reuse in building or modding PCs but also for completely separate projects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While degradation is an obvious problem for PC parts, it's a loss of compatibility that you really have to worry about.

According to recent reports, despite the massive cost sinks that go into building a solid PC, many of the parts can easily be reused. That's a good thing, because with no end in sight for the GPU supply problem, the prices of all electronics will likely continue to be pushed up. Nonetheless, in this era of planned obsolescence, it's not unreasonable to be concerned about the lifetime of PC parts. The good news is that old hardware rarely becomes truly useless. Most components keep working until they physically break, though compatibility gaps and rising software demands can eventually leave them obsolete for modern use.

Recent findings suggest that PC parts aren't only great for reuse in building or modding PCs but also for completely separate projects. An old fan purchased in a job lot could easily find a upcoming life as a desk fan, whereas a slab of RAM you're not using anymore can be turned into easy money. As components like HDDs and SSDs remain expensive, it's important to keep tabs on how long your current hardware could last.

Sources indicate that there are generally two categories of components to go over when looking at hardiness. The first are parts that don't massively hinge on compatibility with platform and demand changes, chiefly fans and PC cases. Simple cooling devices and less complex PC cases will likely last you a decade or more if you're kind to them. You will, of course, need to give them a good clean and the occasional tune-up over time, but they'll likely hold up for a long while before passing the point of no return.

It has been revealed that the question becomes a little tricky with other components. Your CPU and RAM sticks will probably last a good while, potentially well over a decade, if you don't see any dire power surges and avoid extreme temperature conditions. Your motherboard, though it can last more than seven years, is where a lack of compatibility really becomes an concern. Not only do motherboards go out of style every few years, but their increasing complexity brings more and more points of failure, leaving more opportunities for outright breakage. GPUs are in a similar boat, as increasing demands in the gaming space lead to latest GPUs falling out of favor every three to five years.

Industry observers note that there's quite the smorgasbord of factors that go into how long PC components can last — from the type of component in question to how much use they've seen historically. The condition hardware is kept in matters too, as poor storage could lead to battery death or leaks, mold growth, corrosion and much more. So do the materials an item is made from; rubberized vintage tech in particular will likely erode into a sticky mess over time — though even this can be patched up.

It also matters what is meant by obsolescence here; a GPU that still works fine may not be strong enough to run many of today's demanding, less-optimized programs. Since RAM prices are high right now, graphics cards are selling for more too, so you're probably better off selling a GPU that can't keep pace by itself. While most components will keep chugging along unless they're properly broken, a lack of compatibility can bleed through your old tech supply. Even if you don't have any plans to run the latest games, the internet itself might be too demanding for a vintage rig, as modern websites are bloated with ads and animated elements that are far too demanding for ancient CPUs.

Common reasons why some USB ports are red

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While there's no color-coding standard, red USB ports typically indicate these features.
  • It has been revealed that pick a USB port at random and you'll probably see either black, white or blue.
  • Recent findings suggest that an organization known as the USB Implementers Forum sets the specifications of various USB types, but it doesn't determine what ports themselves can look like, so manufacturers are free to apply colors like red however they see fit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While there's no color-coding standard, red USB ports typically indicate these features.

It has been revealed that pick a USB port at random and you'll probably see either black, white or blue. While those colors are fairly standard, red, yellow or purple USB ports have also popped up on some devices. It's often unclear what exactly the color signifies. The unsatisfying yet true answer is "it depends," but it's worth looking into what a red USB port on your device could mean.

Recent findings suggest that an organization known as the USB Implementers Forum sets the specifications of various USB types, but it doesn't determine what ports themselves can look like, so manufacturers are free to apply colors like red however they see fit. Different companies typically stick to one use for each color, though, and they tend to use red to signify a few similar things, including fast speeds and always-on ports.

Industry observers note that in general, red is used on ports of the USB 3.2 or 3.1 Gen 2 standards. Ports of this type can transfer data at up to 20 Gbps, making them some of the fastest ports in common usage. These standards were succeeded by USB4, which can reach speeds of 40 to 80 Gbps, but is only available in USB-C formats, and these are not color-coded. For most purposes, that means a red USB port is likely to indicate the fastest port available on your device.

Industry observers note that red ports can carry other meanings, though. Some manufacturers use red to mark always-on charging ports, which can continue supplying power to connected devices even when your computer is turned off. Red USB ports are usually best suited to SSDs or other storage devices due to their transfer speeds, but they can also be helpful to keep other devices charged overnight.

In a recent development, since colors aren't standardized, red USB ports might not all have the same functionality even on devices from the same manufacturer. The only way to really be sure of what different colors mean without testing every port yourself is to check the manual for the specific device model you're using. While USB 3.2 and always-on ports are both fairly common, they're more likely to show up on higher-end devices like gaming laptops and motherboards than on everyday electronics.

If you can't find a model number or just want some idea of what a port does at a glance, you can also check the port itself for more information. Manufacturers often mark faster ports with the symbol SS to indicate SuperSpeed or use a number to indicate the exact speed. A lightning bolt is commonly used to mark always-on ports, though it's possible that a port with this symbol also offers a higher speed.

Sources indicate that the good news is that the only risk you run by using the wrong colored USB port is not getting the most power out of it. USB ports are made to be backward compatible, so you can plug a cable into a port of an earlier or later USB generation and it will still work, even if it can't take advantage of its highest transfer speeds.

Breaking: Six products and services Google discontinued in 2026

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1172 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here's a rundown of some Google tools that ended up in the graveyard this year.
  • Google is inherently data-driven, and that extends to its products and services as well.
  • According to recent reports, google Assistant has been phased out in favor of Gemini on mobile devices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here's a rundown of some Google tools that ended up in the graveyard this year.

Google is inherently data-driven, and that extends to its products and services as well. The search giant has a tendency to shut down services when it feels they're not serving its broader goals, and this has led to the discontinuation of products as diverse as Google Reader, Google+, Stadia, Google Glass, Google Hangouts and dozens of other utilities over the last 15 years. 2026 is no different, so let's take a look at everything Google discontinued this year.

According to recent reports, google Assistant has been phased out in favor of Gemini on mobile devices. Google initially targeted the end of 2025 for the transition, but pushed the deadline to September, 2026. This means Assistant is no longer available on mobile devices, Wear OS smartwatches, headphones and earbuds, or vehicles using Android Auto projected from a user's phone. It's still usable on older devices like Nest Audio, Nest Mini, the original Google Home, Google Home Max and cars with Google built-in.

Sources indicate that google Assistant debuted in 2016 (in the short-lived chat app Allo, of all things), and was integrated into much of the broader Android ecosystem, including mobile phones, tablets, smart home devices and vehicles. It provided a hands-free way to control smart home lights, play music, call contacts, and look up information on the web. Those tasks will now be handled by Gemini.

Recent findings suggest that the Pixel Tablet was discontinued in September 2026; the link to its listing now takes you to the Google Store's home page, and Google removed tablets as a category from its site navigation. Google's tablet ambitions have felt half-hearted at times, but the Pixel Tablet sought to change that. The tablet debuted in 2023 for $499, and it came with an 11-inch 60Hz LCD panel, decent hardware and reliable battery life. Google sold the tablet for as little as $250 during the 2025 Black Friday sale.

Its key selling point was the included Charging Speaker Dock, which effectively turned the tablet into a Nest Hub Max. The dock contained a dedicated speaker and served as a Cast target, allowing users to cast music and podcasts to the device. With the discontinuation of the Pixel Tablet, Google no longer has a tablet of its own; there were leaks pointing to a successor with a 120Hz panel, but that never materialized. With Google now focusing on Googlebooks, it may be a while before we see another Pixel Tablet.

It has been revealed that google ended production of the Nest Mini and Nest Audio in June 2026, with both products now discontinued. The Nest Mini proved particularly popular after Google confirmed it in 2019 for just $50, and the smart speaker offered an affordable way to interact with Google Assistant and play music or control smart home devices.

Nest Audio debuted in 2020 for $99, serving as the successor to the original Google Home. It featured a fabric design and surprisingly solid audio quality via two drivers — a 75mm woofer and 19mm tweeter — with only the much larger and more expensive Home Max rivaling its sound quality in Google's speaker portfolio.

Industry observers note that even though the Nest Audio and Nest Mini are discontinued, Google will continue providing software updates for the foreseeable future. Google is now positioning the $99 Google Home Speaker as the go-to choice for anyone looking for a smart speaker. The Home Speaker has 360-degree sound, but it comes with a smaller 58mm driver, and features Gemini instead of Google Assistant.

As part of a broader rebranding initiative centered around Google Health, Google turned the Fitbit app into a unified health portal in May 2026. Alongside the change, Google also indicated that it was migrating Google Fit data over to Google Health.

Google is positioning Health as its go-to choice to monitor health and fitness data from existing Fitbit wearables, and newer devices like the Fitbit Air and Fitbit Edge use it from the get-go. Fitbit's Web APIs have also been wound down, so if you're using a Fitbit fitness band or smartwatch, you will need to install and use Google Health to monitor metrics. While Health has a lot of features — including an AI-assisted Health Coach — it lacks the social features that made Fitbit's app stand out.

In January 2026, Google confirmed that it was ending the service, noting that it didn't "provide helpful next steps," and that it would instead focus on "tools that give you more clear, actionable steps to protect your information online." While there are other monitoring services such as Have I Been Pwned, Google's Dark Web Report was notable because it was integrated into your Google account.

Sources indicate that gmailify was a feature that let you use Yahoo, AOL or Outlook email accounts with Gmail and access spam protection, search, automatic sorting and other services available within Google's email service. The feature debuted 10 years ago, but it was discontinued in Q1 2026; existing users will still be able to use it until January 2027, and then it will be wound down.

Recent findings suggest that that noted, Google still lets you access email from third-party accounts within Gmail for Android and iOS, and it uses the standard Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) protocol to fetch mails. The only glitch is that you don't get some of the extras, like spam protection. In a similar move, Google ended the ability to fetch emails from third-party accounts using the Post Office Protocol (POP); you'll have to use the newer IMAP standard to sync your mails going forward.

According to recent reports, in addition to these, Google discontinued several lesser-known initiatives in 2026. Google revealed in July 2026 that the legacy Google Earth Pro desktop app would no longer be available to download after June 25, 2027. If you've used Google Earth Pro in the past and want to continue using it, all you need to do is download and install the app before June 2027, and it will continue to work even after the wind-down. Google is moving its focus to Google Earth on the web and Android/iOS, and while you can still view satellite imagery and Street View for free, it is introducing tiered subscription intends for access to additional data layers.

Sources indicate that also, Steam for Chromebooks, a beta program that allowed people to install Steam games on ChromeOS machines, ended in January 2026. Google shut down Pixel Studio, a dedicated app that launched with the Pixel 9 series and let you create AI-assisted imagery using text prompts, in March 2026. With image generation moving to Gemini, Google is directing users to its latest AI assistant instead. Google clearly likes building new tools and features, and while that means there's always something exciting on the horizon, the downside is that there's no guarantee the service you use today will be available a year or two down the line.

#2751. Building your own mini PC is harder than you would think

Building your own mini PC is harder than you would think

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that building a custom PC is a wonderfully satisfying feeling.
  • According to recent reports, as you may have noticed, there are so many different form factors for cases and unique enclosures.
  • Unlike larger mid- and full-range towers, the mini PC builds tend to focus on a straight-ahead approach with very little wiggle room for frills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Smaller size can mean greater effort.

Recent findings suggest that building a custom PC is a wonderfully satisfying feeling. Even if you've never built one for yourself, it's ingrained itself into the world of content creation and social media so fiercely that everyone has most likely at least watched someone partially build a PC at some point.

According to recent reports, as you may have noticed, there are so many different form factors for cases and unique enclosures. One of the more interesting ones that has been carving out its own funky niche in the market is the mini PC build. Because of the unique form factors and limited space these cases allow, they come with challenges that make a build of this type a bit more difficult than normal.

Unlike larger mid- and full-range towers, the mini PC builds tend to focus on a straight-ahead approach with very little wiggle room for frills. Things that we take for granted in larger builds, like room for maximum airflow or a larger GPU, become pertinent struggles in the mini PC world.

One of the core things to understand upfront about mini PC builds is the case itself. What we know as mini PCs tend to be built within Mini-ITX or microATX cases. For as small as they are, you might think they'd cost significantly less than their larger siblings. In a lot of situations, that's true, but Mini-ITX cases also come in a lot of different types. Some of them offer fun bells and whistles, which can run your bill up before you know it.

A lot of the mainstream mini computers that you can buy from companies, like Apple's Mac mini or certain models of the ASUS NUC, are built with an SoC — a system-on-a-chip that combines a CPU with a GPU — and RAM sometimes soldered into the motherboard itself. Doing something like that isn't really feasible, but you can get fairly close with some commercial cases.

Recent findings suggest that no matter which one you're looking at, it may be reassuring to know that despite their small stature, a lot of them are surprisingly roomy. You're still going to be limited by what the case allows in terms of dimensions and compatibility, but those are all easy to contrast and compare with the official specs or using a site like PCPartPicker to determine if a component will fit in your case.

According to recent reports, the unorthodox shape and size of a lot of mini PC cases means that while it's entirely possible to fill them with a lot of cool stuff, your approach is going to have to be a bit more economical and predetermined. For most of your situations, a mini ITX case will only accommodate a mini-ITX motherboard, while microATX cases will be able to fit in both Mini-ITX and microATX motherboards due to the micro cases being a bit bigger on average.

Recent findings suggest that airflow also becomes something of a problem, as the smaller size of these cases means your internal components have a lot less room to breathe. There's usually very little space once all the guts are mashed inside, and that's especially true if you go for a discrete GPU as opposed to an APU that combines the CPU and the GPU. The prices of most small form factor, or SFF, PC components are also a bit steep.

SFF power supplies, motherboards, CPU coolers and GPUs can all contribute a surprising amount to the final price of a machine, which may make going for a standard ATX build more appealing. Finding all these unique-sized parts isn't even the most challenging glitch when building a mini PC, as the physical build itself can be far more difficult than that of a standard ATX machine.

There's a lot less room, but you also need to be more careful with the actual installation of parts. A standard ATX build can largely be put together in any order, but mini PC builds need to be put together in a specific order due to the part sizes and clearance concerns.

Recent findings suggest that gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg stated Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent users may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

Latest Update: How to calibrate your 3D printer (and why you should)

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Better first layers, fewer failed prints and a few calibration tests worth knowing about.
  • Your 3D printer can spend hours making a part, only for it to detach from the bed halfway through.
  • According to recent reports, an uneven bed, incorrect nozzle height and poorly tuned extrusion can cause adhesion issues, rough surfaces and dimensional inaccuracies in an FDM 3D printer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Better first layers, fewer failed prints and a few calibration tests worth knowing about.

Your 3D printer can spend hours making a part, only for it to detach from the bed halfway through. Worse, the finished piece might look great but refuse to fit where it should. That's a lot of filament down the drain, all because the printer might need calibration.

According to recent reports, an uneven bed, incorrect nozzle height and poorly tuned extrusion can cause adhesion issues, rough surfaces and dimensional inaccuracies in an FDM 3D printer. Calibration can address those problems on both older printers that need manual adjustments and newer models that handle some checks automatically. It's also worth checking calibration after moving your printer, adjusting belts, replacing a nozzle or performing mechanical maintenance.

The calibration process starts with a mechanical check, cleaning, bed leveling, Z-offset adjustments (when applicable) and a first-layer test. E-step calibration (rotation-distance calibration in Klipper) with a heated or printing-temperature hotend is a good indicator on supported printers to see if the extruder is extruding the right amount of filament before flow rate tuning. The temperature towers can then be used to fine-tune filament settings. There is no fixed schedule for recalibration, so repeat the appropriate checks as you change hardware or if print quality begins to deteriorate.

In a recent development, start with the hardware. Set the printer on a stable surface, and if that's in a bedroom or home office, check whether the space is suitable for 3D printing. With the machine powered off and cooled, inspect for loose belts or toolhead components, then clean the build plate according to the manufacturer's instructions. If your desk is wobbly, the Calibrate button won't fix anything.

Then follow your printer's bed-leveling procedure, often labeled Calibration, Leveling or Self-check. Many newer machines from Bambu Lab, Creality, Prusa and Anycubic can measure the bed automatically, something worth considering if you're buying a 3D printer anytime soon. Some models, including the Bambu Lab A1 and Prusa MK4S, can also set the first-layer height automatically. The routines differ by model, so follow your printer's instructions.

Sources indicate that by contrast, certain machines, such as the Elegoo Neptune 4 and some Creality Ender models, have manual adjustment wheels, so they need a little more attention. Follow the manufacturer's leveling instructions, adjusting the wheels until a sheet of paper slides between the nozzle and bed with slight resistance at the specified points. Then run automatic leveling afterward if your printer supports it.

Finally, print a single-layer square. The lines should touch and appear slightly flattened. Visible gaps can indicate that the nozzle is too high, while raised ridges or scraping suggest it's too close. If your printer allows manual Z-offset adjustments, make small changes and repeat the test.

For E-step calibration, measure the filament, set a measured feed and compare the actual feed, making adjustments as necessary. Klipper has an equivalent setting called rotation distance, so before optimizing filament flow, it makes sense to check this.

In a recent development, it's not enough to get the first layer correct. Even filaments made from the same material can behave differently. One temperature or flow setting may be perfect for one spool but cause problems for another. Be sure to check the calibration options in your slicer.

Recent findings suggest that bambu Studio includes Flow Dynamics and Flow Rate tests, while Creality Print and OrcaSlicer have their own calibration tools. PrusaSlicer also lets you adjust the extrusion multiplier. You don't need to switch slicers to run a test print.

It has been revealed that A temperature tower test prints sections at different nozzle temperatures, letting you compare stringing, bridging and surface quality. Some slicers generate these tests automatically, while others require a downloaded model with temperature changes configured manually. Make sure those temperature changes are configured. Otherwise, you've just printed a tower.

Recent findings suggest that flow-rate calibration is done by testing patches for over-extrusion (extruding too much filament, resulting in buildup) or under-extrusion (extruding too little, resulting in gaps). You can also print a 3DBenchy to examine overhangs and details, or a calibration cube to check basic dimensional consistency. But don't start changing motor steps just because a cube measures slightly smaller than expected. Some annoying factors like material shrinkage, extrusion settings and first-layer squish can also affect those measurements, and so can loose belts or other mechanical problems.

Proper flow and pressure-advance tuning can also reduce blobs around layer starts and stops, although the vertical Z-seam's position is primarily controlled through your slicer's seam settings.

But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful fresh features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

Sources indicate that A upcoming feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

With a latest feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

In a recent development, some of the new features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone people. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that eagles running back Saquon Barkley sold his equity stake in Polymarket after NFL rules barred players from holding prediction-market investments. The case sets the league apart from the NBA and MLB, which have signed deals with the exchanges, as the NFL argues at the Supreme Court that sports event contracts are gambling.

Saquon Barkley no longer owns a piece of Polymarket. The Eagles running back sold his equity stake to comply with league rules, he told Front Office Sports in an interview published October 28. It is the first public case of the NFL applying its gambling rules to a player’s prediction-market investment.

Industry observers note that barkley bought into Polymarket before the league told players they could not hold such investments. The NFL goes over endorsement, investment and training rules with players before every season.

According to recent reports, the league has now made clear that its sportsbook restrictions extend to prediction markets. It declined to comment on Barkley’s case specifically. The stance was not new to players. Kalshi and Polymarket were already off-limits to them as endorsers or brand ambassadors in January 2026. At that point, prediction markets were treated as gambling entities under the league’s gambling policy.

Industry observers note that the NFL’s approach puts it at odds with other major leagues. Polymarket became Major League Baseball’s Official Prediction Market Exchange on March 19, 2026. On October 26, 2026, the NBA named both companies its preferred prediction-market exchanges. The agreement gives them rights to league intellectual property and marketing.

Sources indicate that NBA players face far lighter limits. They can hold stakes in the exchanges and appear in their marketing. The line is drawn only at promoting contracts on NBA games.

In a recent development, the split also shuts NFL players out of an industry that leans heavily on their sport. By the league’s own figures, football made up $1.8 billion of prediction-market trading on the season’s first Sunday. That was more than half of the day’s total.

In a recent development, the league is pressing that view at the Supreme Court. On October 8, 2026, it filed an amicus brief supporting Upcoming Jersey’s request for review in Flaherty v. KalshiEX, case No. 26-299. The NFL argued that sports prediction contracts are gambling. In its view, they are not financial swaps under exclusive federal oversight.

Latest Jersey filed its petition on September 2, 2026. It followed an April ruling in which the Third Circuit sided 2-1 with Kalshi. The appeals court found that the CFTC has exclusive oversight of sports-event contracts.

Exclusive: Saquon Barkley tells FOS he was forced to divest his equity stake in Polymarket.

NFL players are not allowed to invest in or endorse gambling or prediction market companies.

— Front Office Sports (@FOS) October 28, 2026.

It has been revealed that many of the NFL’s concerns will be addressed through the CFTC’s ongoing rulemaking, Kalshi spokesperson Elisabeth Diana said. In her view, the agency already has the power to police sports-related event contracts.

The Supreme Court granted Kalshi a 30-day extension to answer Newly introduced Jersey. Its response, originally due October 8, must now be filed by November 9.

Latest Update: This is the best type of wireless earbuds for audio output

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (652 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, wireless earbud design has evolved in leaps and bounds.
  • Our question today is this: What design actually delivers the best sound?
  • In a recent development, considerations include the type of eartips, how buds secure to your ear, and noise cancelation features.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What design actually delivers the best sound?

In a recent development, wireless earbud design has evolved in leaps and bounds. Some of the earliest models would occasionally lose sync between each ear, never mind questions like battery life or sweat resistance. Now, the best wireless earbuds can last an entire workday and will survive the sweatiest gym sessions. You can even use the AirPods Pro 3 as hearing aids.

Our question today is this: What design actually delivers the best sound? The industry has evolved to support many different form factors, but not all of them are actually geared towards fidelity. Some may prioritize maximum comfort, particular environments or simply a consumer price point. Make the wrong choice, and the results can be extremely disappointing.

In a recent development, considerations include the type of eartips, how buds secure to your ear, and noise cancelation features. We'll also explain when it's worth making some sacrifices, since vanilla audio may be better than nothing at all.

According to recent reports, when it comes to form factor, you'll want to begin with in-ear (sometimes referred to as in-canal) earbuds. These provide several major benefits to audio quality over open-ear designs, beginning with passive noise cancellation. You're blocking most of the outside world, although some noise will inevitably seep through. This positioning also maximizes the perceived volume of each bud, which can help you catch more of the nuances in your movies and music. You should even experience better bass response because the buds are directly rattling your ear and the air inside it.

In a recent development, from here, further narrow your search to models with foam or silicone eartips. These boost passive cancellation as well as bass response, the latter by trapping frequencies inside a space with increased air pressure. For this reason, it's vital to find tips that form a tight fit. You can sometimes upgrade to third-party tips if the ones bundled with your buds aren't doing the job. Keep in mind that while foam is preferable for sound quality, it's less than hygienic for workouts because it's harder to clean.

Speaking of fit, it's also notable to choose buds that lock in as securely as possible without becoming painful to wear. When buds are loose, they can break that ever-so-important sound quality seal, even if you have great tips. You don't necessarily need buds with an external clip, but those may help if you want both quality and the freedom to sprint or do hanging crunches.

You'll also want a design with active noise cancellation (ANC). Passive cancellation merely isolates sound. ANC generates "anti-noise," which partly or completely neutralizing the outside world. This is essential not just for hearing quieter elements in your audio, but also for eliminating distractions such as plane engines or nearby conversation.

Industry observers note that some people intentionally choose open-ear or bone conduction earbuds, despite sacrificing significant bass output and noise cancellation. The reason is simple: situational awareness. If you're running or cycling outside, for example, you can't afford to block out ambient noise because you need to be able to hear an engine, horn, siren or yell warning you of imminent danger. Many in-ear ANC products (like AirPods) compensate by offering "transparency" modes, but of course, it's hard to beat direct exposure to your environment.

Bone conduction buds can sometimes operate in conditions where other designs are unusable, such as underwater. Those benefits go out the window with models that add air-based drivers into the mix to improve bass. All bone conduction buds do, however, deliver many frequencies straight to your inner ear, allowing them to remain "pure" despite mixing with ambience.

Industry observers note that you'll probably recognize immediately whether these sacrifices are essential. When in doubt, it's better to default to in-ear ANC buds. There's just no way of recovering the lost fidelity if you opt for something else.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Vaporum and Serenitatis, as well as the Aristarchus Plateau.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Full Moon is just around the corner, and tonight the Moon is looking almost completely illuminated. We're still in the Waxing Gibbous phase for now, but it won't be long before visibility hits 100%.

As of Sunday, Nov. 22, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 92% of its surface visible.

If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Vaporum and Serenitatis, as well as the Aristarchus Plateau. With binoculars, you'll also see the Apennine Mountains, the Gassendi Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 14 and 17 landing spots, and the Rima Ariadaeus.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

According to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a Latest Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

Fresh Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.
